"""Generate what the schema implies: Company/Domains/Areas notes, the rules note and Rowboat's notes.json."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path

from .model import STRUCTURE_TYPES, Schema, TypeDef
from .notes import note_text, slug, split

log = logging.getLogger("ehl_schema.build")

MANAGED = "schema"
RULES_NOTE = "Agent Notes/Vault Schema"
RULES_MARK = "\n\nSchema rules ("
GENERIC_BODY = ("# {Title}\n\n## Summary\n{2-3 sentences.}\n\n## Key facts\n{Substantive facts only. Leave empty if "
                "none.}\n\n## Open items\n{Next steps only. Leave empty if none.}\n")


def _front(schema: Schema, **fields) -> dict:
    return {**fields, "managed_by": MANAGED, "schema_version": schema.version}


def structure_notes(schema: Schema, company: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    notes: dict[str, str] = {}
    domain_links = "\n".join(f"- [[{schema.domain_note(k)}]]" for k in schema.domains)
    notes["Company"] = note_text(
        _front(schema, id="company", type="Company", domain="company", level=0),
        f"# {company}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Company (L0)\n\n## Domains\n{domain_links}\n")
    for key, title in schema.domains.items():
        areas = "\n".join(f"- [[{schema.area_note(a)}]]" for a, d in schema.areas.items() if d == key)
        notes[schema.domain_note(key)] = note_text(
            _front(schema, id=f"domain-{key}", type="Domains", domain=key, level=1, parent="[[Company]]"),
            f"# {title}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Domain (L1)\n**Key:** {key}\n\n## Areas\n{areas}\n")
    for area, key in schema.areas.items():
        types = ", ".join(n for n, td in schema.types.items() if td.default_parent == area) or "none"
        notes[schema.area_note(area)] = note_text(
            _front(schema, id=f"area-{slug(area)}", type="Areas", domain=key, level=2,
                   parent=f"[[{schema.domain_note(key)}]]"),
            f"# {area}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Area (L2)\n**Domain:** [[{schema.domain_note(key)}]]\n"
            f"**Note types placed here by default:** {types}\n")
    td = schema.types["Agent Notes"]
    notes[RULES_NOTE] = note_text(
        _front(schema, id="agent-notes-vault-schema", type="Agent Notes", domain=td.domain, level=td.level,
               parent=f"[[{schema.area_note(td.default_parent)}]]"),
        rules_body(schema))
    return notes


def rules_body(schema: Schema) -> str:
    lines = [f"# Vault schema (v{schema.version})", "",
             "Generated from schema/vault-schema.yaml by `ehl-schema build`. Do not edit; change the schema file.", "",
             "## Front matter", "",
             "Every note starts with flat YAML front matter. Required keys: id, type, domain, level, parent.",
             "- `id`: a stable slug; never change it. `type`: the folder name. `level`: from the table below.",
             '- `parent`: exactly one quoted link, for example `parent: "[[Areas/Pipeline]]"`.',
             '- Relations are lists of quoted links with the full path, for example `about: ["[[Areas/Pipeline]]"]`.',
             "- Never nest keys. Optional: status, visibility (team | restricted), env (prod | test), when (YYYY-MM-DD).",
             "", "## Domains and areas", "", "| Domain | Key | Areas |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for key, title in schema.domains.items():
        areas = ", ".join(a for a, d in schema.areas.items() if d == key)
        lines.append(f"| {title} | {key} | {areas} |")
    lines += ["", "## Note types", "",
              "| Type (folder) | Domain | Level | Parent (in order) | Default area | Required | Optional |",
              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for name, td in schema.types.items():
        if name in STRUCTURE_TYPES:
            continue
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {td.domain} | {td.level} | {', '.join(td.parent)} | {td.default_parent or ''} | "
                     f"{', '.join(td.required) or '–'} | {', '.join(td.optional) or '–'} |")
    lines += ["", "## Relations", "", "| Key | Points to |", "|---|---|"]
    for name, rel in schema.relations.items():
        target = "a date" if rel.kind == "date" else ("any note" if rel.targets is None else ", ".join(rel.targets))
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {target} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def write_structure(schema: Schema, vault: Path, company: str) -> int:
    written = 0
    for path, text in structure_notes(schema, company).items():
        file = vault / f"{path}.md"
        if file.exists():
            old = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            if old == text:
                continue
            front, _, _ = split(old)
            if (front or {}).get("managed_by") != MANAGED:
                log.warning("%s exists and is not managed by the schema; left as it is", file)
                continue
        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        file.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        written += 1
    return written


def _parent_hint(td: TypeDef) -> str:
    if td.parent == ("Areas",):
        return f"Areas/{td.default_parent}"
    options = ", ".join(f"{p}/…" for p in td.parent if p != "Areas")
    return f"one of: {options}" + (f" (else Areas/{td.default_parent})" if td.default_parent else "")


def _skeleton(schema: Schema, td: TypeDef) -> str:
    lines = ["---", "id: {slug of the title}", f"type: {td.name}", f"domain: {td.domain}", f"level: {td.level}",
             f'parent: "[[{{{_parent_hint(td)}}}]]"']
    for name in td.required:
        rel = schema.relations[name]
        if rel.kind == "date":
            lines.append(f"{name}: {{YYYY-MM-DD}}")
        else:
            target = rel.targets[0] if rel.targets else "Folder"
            lines.append(f'{name}: ["[[{{{target}/…}}]]"]')
    lines += [f"schema_version: {schema.version}", "---", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _guide(schema: Schema, td: TypeDef) -> str:
    default = f" (else [[Areas/{td.default_parent}]])" if td.default_parent else ""
    return (f"v{schema.version}): flat YAML front matter. type: {td.name}; domain: {td.domain}; level: {td.level}; "
            f"id: a stable slug, never change it. parent: exactly one quoted link to a note of type "
            f"{', '.join(td.parent)}{default}. Required relations: {', '.join(td.required) or 'none'}. "
            f"Optional relations: {', '.join(td.optional) or 'none'}. Relation values are lists of quoted "
            f'full-path links like ["[[Organizations/Acme]]"]. Status: {", ".join(td.statuses) or "free text"}.')


def _strip_front(template: str) -> str:
    """The template body without a leading --- block. Text-based: template placeholders are not always YAML."""
    t = template.replace("\r\n", "\n")
    if t.startswith("---\n"):
        end = t.find("\n---\n", 3)
        if end != -1:
            return t[end + 5:]
    return t


def notes_json(schema: Schema, existing: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    by_type = {e["type"]: dict(e) for e in existing if isinstance(e, dict) and "type" in e}
    order = [e["type"] for e in existing if isinstance(e, dict) and "type" in e]
    for name, td in schema.types.items():
        if name in STRUCTURE_TYPES or (td.builtin and name not in by_type):
            continue
        entry = by_type.get(name, {"type": name, "folder": name, "template": "", "extractionGuide": ""})
        if name not in by_type:
            order.append(name)
        template = entry.get("template") or ""
        if not (td.builtin and not template.strip()):
            body = _strip_front(template)
            body = body if body.strip() else (td.template or GENERIC_BODY)
            entry["template"] = _skeleton(schema, td) + body
        guide = (entry.get("extractionGuide") or "").split(RULES_MARK)[0]
        entry["extractionGuide"] = guide + RULES_MARK + _guide(schema, td)
        by_type[name] = entry
    return [by_type[name] for name in order]


def build(schema: Schema, workdir: Path, company: str) -> dict:
    written = write_structure(schema, workdir / "knowledge", company)
    config = workdir / "config" / "notes.json"
    if not config.exists():
        log.warning("%s does not exist yet: start Rowboat once, then run build again", config)
        return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "missing"}
    old = config.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    new = json.dumps(notes_json(schema, json.loads(old)), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
    if new == old:
        return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "unchanged"}
    config.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "updated"}

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\User\.claude\plugins\cache\claude-plugins-official\superpowers\6.4.1\skills\finishing-a-development-branch

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## Step 1: Verify Tests

Run the project's full test suite (`npm test` / `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`).

**If tests fail**, report the failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite:

```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]
```

**If tests pass:** continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

The base branch is whatever this work forked from — usually named in the
plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream. If it is not already
known, ask: "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

## Step 5: Execute Choice

### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Get main repo root for CWD safety
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"

# Merge first — verify success before removing anything
git checkout <base-branch>
git pull
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>
```

If tests fail on the merged result: stop, leave the worktree and branch in
place, and investigate — nothing has been pushed, so the merge is local
and recoverable.

Once the merged result is green: clean up the worktree (Step 6), then
delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
# From a detached HEAD, name the new branch on the remote:
# git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch>
```

Then create the pull/merge request against <base-branch> with the forge's
tooling — its CLI if one is available, or the creation URL most forges
print when you push — following the repo's PR template and conventions if
present, and report the URL to your human partner.

Keep the worktree — your human partner iterates on PR feedback there.

### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

### If your human partner asks to discard the work

This path exists only as a response to an explicit request to throw the
work away. Confirm first:

```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for that exact confirmation. When it arrives:

```bash
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"
```

Then clean up the worktree (Step 6) and force-delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

## Step 6: Cleanup Workspace

**Runs for Option 1 and confirmed discards.** Options 2 and 3 always
preserve the worktree. Both callers have already changed directory to the
main repo root — worktree removal must run from outside the worktree —
and use the `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON`/`WORKTREE_PATH` values captured in
Step 2, from before that directory change.

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON`:** Normal repo, no worktree to clean up. Done.

**If `WORKTREE_PATH` is under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`:** Superpowers
created this worktree — we own cleanup:

```bash
git worktree remove "$WORKTREE_PATH"
git worktree prune  # Self-healing: clean up any stale registrations
```

**If removal is refused** (`contains modified or untracked files`): the
worktree holds files that exist nowhere else — uncommitted plans, notes,
or scratch work. Never `--force` on your own initiative. Show your human
partner what is at stake and ask:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" status --porcelain -uall
```

```
Worktree removal refused — these files were never committed:

<file list>

1. Commit them to <branch> before cleanup
2. Move them into <main repo root>
3. Delete them (unrecoverable)

Which?
```

Carry out the choice, then remove the worktree.

**Otherwise:** The host environment owns this workspace — leave it in
place. If your platform provides a workspace-exit tool, use it.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | yes | - | - | yes |
| 2. Create PR | - | yes | yes | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | yes | - |
| Discard (explicit request only) | - | - | - | yes (force) |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Tests passed earlier this session" | Run the suite on the tree you are about to integrate. A green run only proves the tree it ran on. |
| "They obviously want it merged" | Integration is your human partner's decision. Present the menu and wait. |
| "They seem done with this feature — I'll offer to discard it" | The menu is complete as written. Discard happens only when your human partner asks for it in so many words. |
| "'Yeah, get rid of it' counts as confirmation" | Only the typed word `discard` authorizes deletion. |
| "The PR is up, so the worktree is clutter now" | PR feedback gets fixed in that worktree. It stays until the work lands. |
| "This other worktree looks stale — I'll clean it too" | Clean up only worktrees under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`. Everything else belongs to the host. |
| "Removal refused — `--force` is just finishing the cleanup" | The refusal means files exist only in that worktree. `--force` destroys them permanently. Show your human partner and ask. |
| "The merged-result failure is probably flaky" | A failing merged result stops everything. Branch and worktree stay put while you investigate. |
| "The base branch is obviously main" | Confirm the fork point or ask. Merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo. |
| "The push was rejected — force-push will fix it" | A rejected push means the remote moved. Investigate; force-push only on your human partner's explicit request. |

content.text:
To make Rowboat's graph "know" about the hierarchy, two places in the Rowboat fork (`Flissel/rowboat`, branch `ehl`) need to change. Rowboat doesn't need to know about our schema, only about the front matter keys.

**1. The data: `apps/renderer/src/App.tsx`, `buildGraph` (~lines 7040–7150)**

Today it reads every note, finds `[[links]]` anywhere in the file with one regex (~7072), and groups nodes by the first folder in the path (~7098). It would:
- **Parse the front matter.** The renderer already has a parser in `apps/renderer/src/lib/frontmatter.ts`.
- **Put `level`, `parent` and `domain` on each node.** `GraphNode` in `graph-view.tsx` gets three optional fields.
- **Give each edge a kind.** `GraphEdge` gets `kind: 'parent' | 'relation' | 'link'` plus the relation name:
  - `parent` → kind `parent`,
  - `customer`/`owner`/… → kind `relation`,
  - links in the body → kind `link`.
- **Colour by `domain`** instead of by folder.

**2. The layout: `apps/renderer/src/components/graph-view.tsx`**

Today it runs its own force simulation (spring, repulsion and cluster constants, ~lines 36–49 and 211–296). It would get a **hierarchical layout** whenever nodes carry `level` and `parent`:
- **2D, radial:** Company in the centre, one ring per level, each child inside its parent's angular sector, sized by its subtree.
- **Edge styles:** `parent` edges solid, relations dashed, body links faint and switchable.
- **Fallback:** vaults without front matter keep today's force layout, so other Rowboat users lose nothing.

**3. Optional, the actual 3D/octree view**
- three.js and react-three-fiber as new renderer dependencies. They're already used in our `demo/visu`, but not in Rowboat.
- Each subtree becomes a box nested inside its parent's box, with levels as depth.
- Bigger change: new dependency, camera and controls, picking.

**My recommendation:** do it in two steps.
- **Step A:** 1 + 2 (2D radial). About two files, no new dependency, and you see the hierarchy right away.
- **Step B:** 3 (3D) on top, reusing the same node and edge data.

This is sub-project 2. It changes Rowboat itself, so it needs a branch in your fork and a PR into `Flissel/rowboat:ehl`, and `why-rowboat.md` must stop saying "unmodified". Should I start the design for step A (short brainstorming, then spec and plan)?

The branch question for sub-project 1 is still open: 1 merge to `main` locally, 2 create a PR, 3 keep as is.

# Imagine — Visual Creation Suite ## Modules Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance: - `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams - `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards - `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls - `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth) - `art` — illustration and generative art Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance. **Complexity budget — hard limits:** - Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box. - Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp. - Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams. If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything. **Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `

` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.) You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat. ## Core Design System These rules apply to ALL use cases. ### Philosophy - **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins. - **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces. - **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text. - **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. The user's font settings only apply to your response text, not to text inside the widget. ### Streaming Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early. - **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last. - **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately. - Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream. - Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS. - Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead. ### Rules - No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming) - No font-size below 11px - No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths. - No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects - No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg) - **Typography**: The default font is Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-voice)`. - **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI. - **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings. - **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only. - The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element. - Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style="min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;">` and put the modal inside — it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height. - **Fullscreen / expand buttons**: there is no fullscreen. Never call any element's `requestFullscreen()`, never call `document.exitFullscreen()`, and never key state on `document.fullscreenElement` (the API is dead inside the widget iframe and `fullscreenElement` stays null forever, so a label or branch keyed on it is permanently stuck), never call display-mode host APIs, and never fake fullscreen by restyling your container to viewport size — all of these produce dead or broken controls on at least one platform. If the user asks for a fullscreen or expand button, implement an expanded-layout toggle instead: a synchronous CSS class flip on in-flow content with explicit px sizes (taller chart, roomier controls), updating the button label in the same handler — no async, no awaits, symmetric enter/exit. Mutate the existing elements' classes and text; never rebuild the control's DOM with innerHTML (replacement silently drops event listeners and leaves a dead button). The host resizes to fit your content automatically. - No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` — just content fragments. - When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text — never plain black or generic gray. - **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--radius)` for controls, `12px` for cards. In SVG, `rx="4"` is the default — larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill. - **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** — if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides. - **No titles or prose inside the tool output** — see Philosophy above. - **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class="ti …">` sizes with `font-size` — 16–20px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits). - No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming — hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine — see Illustrative/Interactive sections.) - No nested scrolling — auto-fit height. - **Validate input in interactive widgets.** Any widget that collects user input before acting on it (quiz answers, text boxes, form fields) must check that input in its submit handler: if a required field is empty or invalid, show a clear inline error next to the control (13px `color: var(--text-danger)` text, e.g. "Enter an answer first") and stop — do not advance to the next step, reveal the answer, or otherwise proceed until the input is valid. Clear the error as soon as the user edits the field. - Scripts execute after streaming — load libraries via `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows. The library `<script src>` tag must come BEFORE any inline script that uses its global — never call a library from code that appears above its `<script src>` tag. - **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external resources may ONLY load from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`. All other origins are blocked by the sandbox — the request silently fails. ### CSS Variables **Surfaces**: `--surface-2` (white), `--surface-1` (card), `--surface-0` (page bg); role tints `--bg-{accent,danger,success,warning}` **Text**: `--text-primary` (black), `--text-secondary` (muted), `--text-muted` (hints); role `--text-{accent,danger,success,warning}` **Borders**: `--border` (default hairline), `--border-strong` (hover), `--border-stronger`; role `--border-{accent,danger,success,warning}` **Typography**: `--font-sans`, `--font-voice` (serif), `--font-mono` **Layout**: `--radius` (8px), `--pad-{sm,md,lg,xl}`, `--gap-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`; for larger corners use literal `12px`/`16px` All auto-adapt to light/dark mode. For custom colors in HTML, use CSS variables. **Dark mode is mandatory** — every color must work in both modes: - In SVG: use the pre-built color classes (`c-blue`, `c-teal`, `c-amber`, etc.) for colored nodes — they handle light/dark mode automatically. Never write `<style>` blocks for colors. - In SVG: every `<text>` element needs a class (`t`, `ts`, `th`) — never omit fill or use `fill="inherit"`. Inside a `c-{color}` parent, text classes auto-adjust to the ramp. - In HTML: always use CSS variables (--text-primary, --text-secondary) for text. Never hardcode colors like color: #333 — invisible in dark mode. - Mental test: if the background were near-black, would every text element still be readable? ### sendPrompt(text) A global function that sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. Use it when the user's next step benefits from Claude thinking. Handle filtering, sorting, toggling, and calculations in JS instead. ### Links `<a href="https://...">` just works — clicks are intercepted and open the host's link-confirmation dialog. Or call `openLink(url)` directly. ## When nothing fits Pick the closest use case below and adapt. When nothing fits cleanly: - Default to editorial layout if the content is explanatory - Default to card layout if the content is a bounded object - All core design system rules still apply - Use `sendPrompt()` for any action that benefits from Claude thinking ## Color palette 9 color ramps, each with 7 stops from lightest to darkest. 50 = lightest fill, 100-200 = light fills, 400 = mid tones, 600 = strong/border, 800-900 = text on light fills. | Class | Ramp | 50 (lightest) | 100 | 200 | 400 | 600 | 800 | 900 (darkest) | |-------|------|------|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|------| | `c-purple` | Purple | #EEEDFE | #CECBF6 | #AFA9EC | #7F77DD | #534AB7 | #3C3489 | #26215C | | `c-teal` | Teal | #E1F5EE | #9FE1CB | #5DCAA5 | #1D9E75 | #0F6E56 | #085041 | #04342C | | `c-coral` | Coral | #FAECE7 | #F5C4B3 | #F0997B | #D85A30 | #993C1D | #712B13 | #4A1B0C | | `c-pink` | Pink | #FBEAF0 | #F4C0D1 | #ED93B1 | #D4537E | #993556 | #72243E | #4B1528 | | `c-gray` | Gray | #F1EFE8 | #D3D1C7 | #B4B2A9 | #888780 | #5F5E5A | #444441 | #2C2C2A | | `c-blue` | Blue | #E6F1FB | #B5D4F4 | #85B7EB | #378ADD | #185FA5 | #0C447C | #042C53 | | `c-green` | Green | #EAF3DE | #C0DD97 | #97C459 | #639922 | #3B6D11 | #27500A | #173404 | | `c-amber` | Amber | #FAEEDA | #FAC775 | #EF9F27 | #BA7517 | #854F0B | #633806 | #412402 | | `c-red` | Red | #FCEBEB | #F7C1C1 | #F09595 | #E24B4A | #A32D2D | #791F1F | #501313 | **How to assign colors**: Color should encode meaning, not sequence. Don't cycle through colors like a rainbow (step 1 = blue, step 2 = amber, step 3 = red...). Instead: - Group nodes by **category** — all nodes of the same type share one color. E.g. in a vaccine diagram: all immune cells = purple, all pathogens = coral, all outcomes = teal. - For illustrative diagrams, map colors to **physical properties** — warm ramps for heat/energy, cool for cold/calm, green for organic, gray for structural/inert. - Use **gray for neutral/structural** nodes (start, end, generic steps). - Use **2-3 colors per diagram**, not 6+. More colors = more visual noise. A diagram with gray + purple + teal is cleaner than one using every ramp. - **Prefer purple, teal, coral, pink** for general diagram categories. Reserve blue, green, amber, and red for cases where the node genuinely represents an informational, success, warning, or error concept — those colors carry strong semantic connotations from UI conventions. (Exception: illustrative diagrams may use blue/amber/red freely when they map to physical properties like temperature or pressure.) **Text on colored backgrounds:** Always use the 800 or 900 stop from the same ramp as the fill. Never use black, gray, or --text-primary on colored fills. **When a box has both a title and a subtitle, they must be two different stops** — title darker (800 in light mode, 100 in dark), subtitle lighter (600 in light, 200 in dark). Same stop for both reads flat; the weight difference alone isn't enough. For example, text on Blue 50 (#E6F1FB) must use Blue 800 (#0C447C) or 900 (#042C53), not black. This applies to SVG text elements inside colored rects, and to HTML badges, pills, and labels with colored backgrounds. **Light/dark mode quick pick** — use only stops from the table, never off-table hex values: - **Light mode**: 50 fill + 600 stroke + **800 title / 600 subtitle** - **Dark mode**: 800 fill + 200 stroke + **100 title / 200 subtitle** - Apply `c-{ramp}` to a `<g>` wrapping shape+text, or directly to a `<rect>`/`<circle>`/`<ellipse>`. Never to `<path>` — paths don't get ramp fill. For colored connector strokes use inline `stroke="#..."` (any mid-ramp hex works in both modes). Dark mode is automatic for ramp classes. Available: c-gray, c-blue, c-red, c-amber, c-green, c-teal, c-purple, c-coral, c-pink. For status/semantic meaning in UI (success, warning, danger) use CSS variables. For categorical coloring in both diagrams and UI, use these ramps. ## SVG setup **ViewBox safety checklist** — before finalizing any SVG, verify: 1. Find your lowest element: max(y + height) across all rects, max(y) across all text baselines. 2. Set viewBox height = that value + 40px buffer. 3. Find your rightmost element: max(x + width) across all rects. All content must stay within x=0 to x=680. 4. For text with text-anchor="end", the text extends LEFT from x. If x=118 and text is 200px wide, it starts at x=-82 — outside the viewBox. Increase x or use text-anchor="start". 5. Never use negative x or y coordinates. The viewBox starts at 0,0. 6. **No unintentional overlaps.** For every pair of elements that aren't meant to layer (label-on-label, label-on-arrow, box-on-box, callout-on-shape), check their bounding boxes do not intersect. The only allowed overlaps are deliberate: a label centered inside its own box, an arrowhead touching the box it points to, a highlight rect behind the thing it highlights. If two unrelated elements would collide, move one — shorten the label, shift the y, add a row. A diagram with crossed labels reads as broken regardless of how good the content is. 7. Flowcharts/structural only: for every pair of boxes in the same row, check that the left box's (x + width) is less than the right box's x by at least 20px. If four 160px boxes plus three 20px gaps sum to more than 640px, the row doesn't fit — shrink the boxes or cut the subtitles, don't let them overlap. **SVG setup**: `<svg width="100%" viewBox="0 0 680 H" role="img"><title>………` — 680px wide, flexible height. # Rowboat brain graph: hierarchical layout (sub-project 2, step A)

**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** draft for review
**Depends on:** the vault schema, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-vault-schema-design.md` (sub-project 1).
**Changes:** the Rowboat fork `Flissel/rowboat`, branch `ehl` (upstream `72e9d8c`), through a PR from
`ehl/schema-graph`.

## 1. Goal

Rowboat's brain graph shows the vault hierarchy that sub-project 1 wrote into every note's front matter
(`level`, `parent`, `domain`, typed relations). The graph keeps its floating, draggable force layout.

Notes are pulled onto **one ring per level** around the company note in the centre. Each subtree stays in
its parent's angular sector.

**Success criteria**

- On the EHL vault (`~/.rowboat-ehl`, 288 notes):
  - The company note sits in the centre and the 15 domains form the first ring.
  - Every area sits on the second ring, in its domain's sector.
  - Every note sits on the ring of its level, near its parent.
- Parent edges, relation edges and body links look different from each other.
- Colours and the legend follow `domain`.
- A vault without `level`/`parent` front matter looks and behaves exactly as today.
- New logic sits in a pure, unit-tested module. The vitest suite of the renderer stays green.

## 2. Current code (Rowboat `72e9d8c`)

| Place | Today |
|---|---|
| `apps/renderer/src/App.tsx` `buildGraph` (~7040–7150) | Reads every note except `Meetings/`. Finds `[[links]]` in the whole text with one regex and stores them as undirected, untyped edges. Groups nodes by the first path segment and colours them by group index. |
| `apps/renderer/src/components/graph-view.tsx` | `GraphNode {id, label, degree, radius, group, color, stroke}`, `GraphEdge {source, target}`. Own simulation (~200–300): 240 steps of repulsion, edge springs (`SPRING_LENGTH 80`), a pull to group centres placed on a circle, damping. World origin (0,0) is the view centre. SVG lines for edges (~535), circles and labels for nodes. The legend comes from groups. |
| `apps/renderer/src/lib/frontmatter.ts` | `splitFrontmatter(content)` and `extractAllFrontmatterValues(raw)`. The latter returns flow lists like `["[[A]]"]` as raw strings and quoted values with their quotes. |

## 3. Design

### 3.1 New pure module `apps/renderer/src/lib/graph-hierarchy.ts`

```ts
export type Relation = { name: string; target: string }        // target: vault path without ".md"
export type Hierarchy = { level?: number; parent?: string; domain?: string; relations: Relation[] }

export function parseHierarchy(content: string): Hierarchy
export function hierarchyForces(
  nodes: { id: string; level?: number; parentId?: string }[],
  positions: Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>,
  params?: { ringSpacing?: number; ringStrength?: number; angleStrength?: number },
): Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>
```

**`parseHierarchy`**
- Uses `splitFrontmatter`.
- Reads the flat keys `level` (integer), `parent` and `domain`. `parent` is one link, quoted or not, with
  `|alias` and `#heading` stripped. `domain` is a string.
- Every other key whose value is a list of links becomes relations, e.g. `customer: ["[[Organizations/Acme]]"]`.
- Not relations: `parent`, and keys whose values are not links.
- Accepts CRLF.
- A note without front matter gives `{ relations: [] }`.

**`hierarchyForces`** returns an extra force per node:
- **Ring force:** pulls a node with `level` radially toward radius `level × ringSpacing` around (0, 0).
  - Default `ringSpacing` 140, strength 0.02.
  - Level 0 is pulled to the centre.
- **Parent-angle force:** pulls a node with a positioned parent tangentially toward the parent's angle, at
  the node's own radius. Default strength 0.015.
- **No `level`:** the node gets no force.

### 3.2 `App.tsx`, `buildGraph`

- **Parse every note once.** For each note in `contents`, call `parseHierarchy(data)`.
- **Nodes** get `level`, `parentId` and `domain`. `parentId` is set only if the target is a node of the graph.
- **Edges** get `kind: 'parent' | 'relation' | 'link'` and an optional `relation` name.
  - The parent link gives a `parent` edge; relations give `relation` edges; other `[[links]]` give `link`
    edges.
  - One edge per unordered pair, as today. The strongest kind wins: parent > relation > link.
- **Group and colour:** when the node has a `domain`, group = `domain`. Otherwise today's first-folder group
  is used. The palette and depth shading are unchanged.

### 3.3 `graph-view.tsx`

- **Types:**
  - `GraphNode` gets optional `level?: number`, `parentId?: string`, `domain?: string`.
  - `GraphEdge` gets optional `kind?: 'parent' | 'relation' | 'link'` and `relation?: string`.
  - All fields are optional, so other callers keep compiling.
- **Hierarchy mode** is on when at least one node has a `level`.
  - **Initial positions:** a node with `level` starts on its ring. Its angle is spread over its parent's
    sector (siblings evenly), or over the full circle for level ≤ 1.
  - **Each step:** nodes with `level` get `hierarchyForces` instead of the group-centre pull. Repulsion,
    edge springs, damping and dragging stay.
  - **Edge springs:** the spring length is `ringSpacing` for `parent` edges and today's 80 for others.
  - **Rings:** faint background circles at each used level radius.
- **Edge style:**

| Kind | Opacity | Dash |
|---|---|---|
| `parent` | 0.5 | solid |
| `relation` | 0.45 | dash `4 3`; `<title>` shows the relation name |
| `link` | 0.12 | solid |

  Hover, search and group highlighting keep today's rules on top of this.
- **Legend** shows domains (group labels) as today.
- **Off:** when hierarchy mode is off, the code paths are exactly the current ones.

## 4. Testing

- **`apps/renderer/src/lib/graph-hierarchy.test.ts` (vitest):**
  - `parseHierarchy`:
    - quoted and unquoted parent
    - alias and heading stripped
    - flow lists → relations
    - non-link keys ignored
    - CRLF
    - no front matter
    - level parsed as a number
  - `hierarchyForces`:
    - a node outside its ring gets a force toward the centre, a node inside gets one outward
    - a child at a different angle than its parent gets a tangential force toward the parent's side
    - a node without a level gets no force
    - level 0 is pulled toward (0, 0)
- **Renderer suite:** `pnpm --filter @x/renderer test` (or the package's `vitest run`) stays green.
- **Manual check:**
  - Run Rowboat in dev mode with `ROWBOAT_WORKDIR=~/.rowboat-ehl`.
  - Open Brain → Graph. Check the success criteria in §1 with a screenshot.
  - Switch to a vault without schema front matter (`~/.rowboat`) and check that the old layout is unchanged.

## 5. Delivery

- **Branch:** `ehl/schema-graph` in `C:/Users/User/Desktop/rowboat` (remote `origin` = `Flissel/rowboat`), from `ehl`.
- **PR:** into `Flissel/rowboat:ehl`.
- **Docs:** this repo's `docs/why-rowboat.md` says "unmodified". It changes to "one small, named patch: the
  hierarchical brain graph (`Flissel/rowboat` PR #…)" in the same delivery. The README licence line and
  NOTICE change the same way: one file group modified, Apache 2.0 §4(b) notice in the changed files' header
  comment.

## 6. Out of scope

- 3D / octree view (step B).
- Editing parents in the graph.
- Agent changes (sub-project 3).
- Business-data bridges (sub-project 4).
- Showing `Meetings/` in the graph (still excluded, as today).

# Rowboat brain graph: hierarchical layout (sub-project 2, step A)

**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** draft for review
**Depends on:** the vault schema, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-vault-schema-design.md` (sub-project 1).
**Changes:** the Rowboat fork `Flissel/rowboat`, branch `ehl` (upstream `72e9d8c`), through a PR from
`ehl/schema-graph`.

## 1. Goal

Rowboat's brain graph shows the vault hierarchy that sub-project 1 wrote into every note's front matter
(`level`, `parent`, `domain`, typed relations). The graph keeps its floating, draggable force layout.

Notes are pulled onto **one ring per level** around the company note in the centre. Each subtree stays in
its parent's angular sector.

**Success criteria**

- On the EHL vault (`~/.rowboat-ehl`, 288 notes):
  - The company note sits in the centre and the 15 domains form the first ring.
  - Every area sits on the second ring, in its domain's sector.
  - Every note sits on the ring of its level, near its parent.
- Parent edges, relation edges and body links look different from each other.
- Colours and the legend follow `domain`.
- A vault without `level`/`parent` front matter looks and behaves exactly as today.
- New logic sits in a pure, unit-tested module. The vitest suite of the renderer stays green.

## 2. Current code (Rowboat `72e9d8c`)

| Place | Today |
|---|---|
| `apps/renderer/src/App.tsx` `buildGraph` (~7040–7150) | Reads every note except `Meetings/`. Finds `[[links]]` in the whole text with one regex and stores them as undirected, untyped edges. Groups nodes by the first path segment and colours them by group index. |
| `apps/renderer/src/components/graph-view.tsx` | `GraphNode {id, label, degree, radius, group, color, stroke}`, `GraphEdge {source, target}`. Own simulation (~200–300): 240 steps of repulsion, edge springs (`SPRING_LENGTH 80`), a pull to group centres placed on a circle, damping. World origin (0,0) is the view centre. SVG lines for edges (~535), circles and labels for nodes. The legend comes from groups. |
| `apps/renderer/src/lib/frontmatter.ts` | `splitFrontmatter(content)` and `extractAllFrontmatterValues(raw)`. The latter returns flow lists like `["[[A]]"]` as raw strings and quoted values with their quotes. |

## 3. Design

### 3.1 New pure module `apps/renderer/src/lib/graph-hierarchy.ts`

```ts
export type Relation = { name: string; target: string }        // target: vault path without ".md"
export type Hierarchy = { level?: number; parent?: string; domain?: string; relations: Relation[] }

export function parseHierarchy(content: string): Hierarchy
export function hierarchyForces(
  nodes: { id: string; level?: number; parentId?: string }[],
  positions: Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>,
  params?: { ringSpacing?: number; ringStrength?: number; angleStrength?: number },
): Map<string, { x: number; y: number }>
```

**`parseHierarchy`**
- Uses `splitFrontmatter`.
- Reads the flat keys `level` (integer), `parent` and `domain`. `parent` is one link, quoted or not, with
  `|alias` and `#heading` stripped. `domain` is a string.
- Every other key whose value is a list of links becomes relations, e.g. `customer: ["[[Organizations/Acme]]"]`.
- Not relations: `parent`, and keys whose values are not links.
- Accepts CRLF.
- A note without front matter gives `{ relations: [] }`.

**`hierarchyForces`** returns an extra force per node:
- **Ring force:** pulls a node with `level` radially toward radius `level × ringSpacing` around (0, 0).
  - Default `ringSpacing` 140, strength 0.02.
  - Level 0 is pulled to the centre.
- **Parent-angle force:** pulls a node with a positioned parent tangentially toward the parent's angle, at
  the node's own radius. Default strength 0.015.
- **No `level`:** the node gets no force.

### 3.2 `App.tsx`, `buildGraph`

- **Parse every note once.** For each note in `contents`, call `parseHierarchy(data)`.
- **Nodes** get `level`, `parentId` and `domain`. `parentId` is set only if the target is a node of the graph.
- **Edges** get `kind: 'parent' | 'relation' | 'link'` and an optional `relation` name.
  - The parent link gives a `parent` edge; relations give `relation` edges; other `[[links]]` give `link`
    edges.
  - One edge per unordered pair, as today. The strongest kind wins: parent > relation > link.
- **Group and colour:** when the node has a `domain`, group = `domain`. Otherwise today's first-folder group
  is used. The palette and depth shading are unchanged.

### 3.3 `graph-view.tsx`

- **Types:**
  - `GraphNode` gets optional `level?: number`, `parentId?: string`, `domain?: string`.
  - `GraphEdge` gets optional `kind?: 'parent' | 'relation' | 'link'` and `relation?: string`.
  - All fields are optional, so other callers keep compiling.
- **Hierarchy mode** is on when at least one node has a `level`.
  - **Initial positions:** a node with `level` starts on its ring. Its angle is spread over its parent's
    sector (siblings evenly), or over the full circle for level ≤ 1.
  - **Each step:** nodes with `level` get `hierarchyForces` instead of the group-centre pull. Repulsion,
    edge springs, damping and dragging stay.
  - **Edge springs:** the spring length is `ringSpacing` for `parent` edges and today's 80 for others.
  - **Rings:** faint background circles at each used level radius.
- **Edge style:**

| Kind | Opacity | Dash |
|---|---|---|
| `parent` | 0.5 | solid |
| `relation` | 0.45 | dash `4 3`; `<title>` shows the relation name |
| `link` | 0.12 | solid |

  Hover, search and group highlighting keep today's rules on top of this.
- **Legend** shows domains (group labels) as today.
- **Off:** when hierarchy mode is off, the code paths are exactly the current ones.

## 4. Testing

- **`apps/renderer/src/lib/graph-hierarchy.test.ts` (vitest):**
  - `parseHierarchy`:
    - quoted and unquoted parent
    - alias and heading stripped
    - flow lists → relations
    - non-link keys ignored
    - CRLF
    - no front matter
    - level parsed as a number
  - `hierarchyForces`:
    - a node outside its ring gets a force toward the centre, a node inside gets one outward
    - a child at a different angle than its parent gets a tangential force toward the parent's side
    - a node without a level gets no force
    - level 0 is pulled toward (0, 0)
- **Renderer suite:** `pnpm --filter @x/renderer test` (or the package's `vitest run`) stays green.
- **Manual check:**
  - Run Rowboat in dev mode with `ROWBOAT_WORKDIR=~/.rowboat-ehl`.
  - Open Brain → Graph. Check the success criteria in §1 with a screenshot.
  - Switch to a vault without schema front matter (`~/.rowboat`) and check that the old layout is unchanged.

## 5. Delivery

- **Branch:** `ehl/schema-graph` in `C:/Users/User/Desktop/rowboat` (remote `origin` = `Flissel/rowboat`), from `ehl`.
- **PR:** into `Flissel/rowboat:ehl`.
- **Docs:** this repo's `docs/why-rowboat.md` says "unmodified". It changes to "one small, named patch: the
  hierarchical brain graph (`Flissel/rowboat` PR #…)" in the same delivery. The README licence line and
  NOTICE change the same way: one file group modified, Apache 2.0 §4(b) notice in the changed files' header
  comment.

## 6. Out of scope

- 3D / octree view (step B).
- Editing parents in the graph.
- Agent changes (sub-project 3).
- Business-data bridges (sub-project 4).
- Showing `Meetings/` in the graph (still excluded, as today).

content.content:
Torque is the decision cockpit, and it runs inside [Rowboat](https://github.com/rowboatlabs/rowboat). Rowboat
is an open-source AI coworker by RowBoat Labs under the Apache License 2.0. This page explains why we built on
Rowboat instead of writing our own shell, and how we connect to it without changing a line of its code.

## Integrated, not forked

The team fork [`Flissel/rowboat`](https://github.com/Flissel/rowboat), branch `ehl`, points at upstream
commit **`72e9d8c`** (9 Oct 2026) with **no changes**. Neither the team fork nor any member's fork has a
commit or pull request on top of upstream. The fork exists only to pin a reproducible base. Everything we
built connects through Rowboat's documented extension points:

| Extension point | What we put there | Written by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<workdir>/apps/torque` (a link to `demo/torque`) | The Torque app with its manifest `rowboat-app.json` (`entry: index.html`, capability `llm`) | `scripts/install.py` |
| `<workdir>/knowledge/` | Notes: `Brands/`, `Models/`, `Components/` (56 car parts), `Feature Classes/`, `Assumptions/`, `Requirements/`, `Purchase Drivers/`, `Data/BMW Dataset.xlsx` | `demo/visu/vault.py notes`, `demo/torque/sync.py` |
| `<workdir>/config/notes.json` | Our note types, each with a template and an extraction guide | `demo/visu/brand.py` (via `vault.py notes`) |
| `<workdir>/config/mcp.json` | The `ehl-market` server (stdio, `python -m ehl_market.server`) | `scripts/install.py` |
| App host API | `/_rowboat/data/*` stores Torque's state and logo; `/_rowboat/llm/generate` serves Nordi and the Concept 3D design prompt | `demo/torque/dist/index.html`, `demo/visu/src/lib/interpret.ts` |

What this gives us:

- **We can upgrade.** A newer Rowboat only needs a new pin. There is no patch set to rebase.
- **Clear authorship.** Everything the team wrote sits in this repository. Rowboat's code is untouched,
  so the jury can see exactly what is ours.
- **Simple licence compliance.** We do not distribute modified Rowboat files, so Apache 2.0 §4(b) (state your
  changes) never applies. We keep Rowboat's licence and credit, list it in [NOTICE](../NOTICE), and do not
  use its name to suggest endorsement (§6).

## What we tried and left out
Rowboat - https://github.com/rowboatlabs/rowboat
  Copyright RowBoat Labs. Apache License 2.0.

Torque is the decision cockpit, and it runs inside [Rowboat](https://github.com/rowboatlabs/rowboat). Rowboat
is an open-source AI coworker by RowBoat Labs under the Apache License 2.0. This page explains why we built on
Rowboat instead of writing our own shell, and how we connect to it without changing a line of its code.

## Integrated, not forked

The team fork [`Flissel/rowboat`](https://github.com/Flissel/rowboat), branch `ehl`, points at upstream
commit **`72e9d8c`** (9 Oct 2026) with **no changes**. Neither the team fork nor any member's fork has a
commit or pull request on top of upstream. The fork exists only to pin a reproducible base. Everything we
built connects through Rowboat's documented extension points:

| Extension point | What we put there | Written by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<workdir>/apps/torque` (a link to `demo/torque`) | The Torque app with its manifest `rowboat-app.json` (`entry: index.html`, capability `llm`) | `scripts/install.py` |
| `<workdir>/knowledge/` | Notes: `Brands/`, `Models/`, `Components/` (56 car parts), `Feature Classes/`, `Assumptions/`, `Requirements/`, `Purchase Drivers/`, `Data/BMW Dataset.xlsx` | `demo/visu/vault.py notes`, `demo/torque/sync.py` |
| `<workdir>/config/notes.json` | Our note types, each with a template and an extraction guide | `demo/visu/brand.py` (via `vault.py notes`) |
| `<workdir>/config/mcp.json` | The `ehl-market` server (stdio, `python -m ehl_market.server`) | `scripts/install.py` |
| App host API | `/_rowboat/data/*` stores Torque's state and logo; `/_rowboat/llm/generate` serves Nordi and the Concept 3D design prompt | `demo/torque/dist/index.html`, `demo/visu/src/lib/interpret.ts` |

What this gives us:

- **We can upgrade.** A newer Rowboat only needs a new pin. There is no patch set to rebase.
- **Clear authorship.** Everything the team wrote sits in this repository. Rowboat's code is untouched,
  so the jury can see exactly what is ours.
- **Simple licence compliance.** We do not distribute modified Rowboat files, so Apache 2.0 §4(b) (state your
  changes) never applies. We keep Rowboat's licence and credit, list it in [NOTICE](../NOTICE), and do not
  use its name to suggest endorsement (§6).

The code changes happen in your Rowboat clone on the new branch `ehl/schema-graph`. The plan has five tasks:
1. **`parseHierarchy`** reads `level`, `parent`, `domain` and the relations from the front matter (8 tests).
2. **Forces and start positions:** a ring force, a pull toward the parent's angle, and start positions inside the parent's sector. Parent cycles can't make it loop forever (7 tests).
3. **Typed edges** (`buildHierarchyGraph`, 4 tests) are wired into `buildGraph`. Nodes get `level`, `parentId` and `domain`, and colours follow the domain.
4. **Hierarchy mode in `graph-view.tsx`:** start on the rings, extra forces, faint rings, dashed relations with their name on hover, faint body links. Then I check it by hand in the running app: does the EHL vault show the hierarchy, and does an old vault look unchanged?
5. **PR into `Flissel/rowboat:ehl`.** `why-rowboat.md`, README, NOTICE and the walkthrough change from "unmodified" to "one marked patch".

I already ran the renderer tests once here; they pass, so vitest works in this environment.

**Execution:** I recommend doing it **myself in this session**, as with sub-project 1. The logic sits in one pure module with 19 tests, the UI change is small, and a fresh reviewer checks everything at the end.

**Does the plan fit, and shall I start that way?**

The hierarchical graph is built and committed in your Rowboat clone on the branch `ehl-schema-graph` (4 commits). Nothing is pushed yet. Before I open the PR, you need to look at it once in the running app.

**Checked so far:**

- Rowboat is still running in dev mode on the vault `~/.rowboat-ehl`. Vite should have reloaded the changed graph by itself; if not, press Ctrl+R in the Rowboat window.

What you should see:
- **Company** in the centre.
- The **15 domains** on the first ring.

- **Dashed** relation lines; if you hover over one, its name appears.
- Very faint body links.
- A legend that lists domains instead of folders.

**Two things I had to decide on the way:**

entries.description: Execute a sequence of actions in ONE tool call. Each individual tool call requires a model→API round trip (seconds); batching a predictable sequence eliminates all but one. Use this whenever you can predict the outcome of several actions ahead — e.g. click a field, type into it, press Return. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error. The frontmost application must be in the session allowlist at the time of this call, or this tool returns an error and does nothing. The frontmost check runs before EACH action inside the batch — if an action opens a non-allowed app, the next action's gate fires and the batch stops there. Screenshot and zoom actions are allowed and their images are returned interleaved with the per-action outputs. Coordinates you write in THIS batch — clicks AND zoom regions — always refer to the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this call, never to a zoom and never to a mid-batch screenshot. After the batch returns, the most recent full screenshot it produced becomes the new coordinate reference for your next call.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__teach_batch
entries.description: Queue multiple teach steps in one tool call. Parallels computer_batch: N steps → one model↔API round trip instead of N. Each step still shows a tooltip and waits for the user's Next click, but YOU aren't waiting for a round trip between steps. You can call teach_batch multiple times in one tour — treat each batch as one predictable SEGMENT (typically: all the steps on one page). The returned screenshot shows the state after the batch's final actions; anchor the NEXT teach_batch against it. WITHIN a batch, all anchors and click coordinates refer to the PRE-BATCH screenshot (same invariant as computer_batch) — for steps 2+ in a batch, either omit anchor (centered tooltip) or target elements you know won't have moved. Good pattern: batch 5 tooltips on page A (last step navigates) → read returned screenshot → batch 3 tooltips on page B → done. Returns {exited:true, stepsCompleted:N} if the user clicks Exit — do NOT call again after that; {stepsCompleted, stepFailed, ...} if an action errors mid-batch; otherwise {stepsCompleted, results:[...]} plus a final screenshot. Fall back to individual teach_step calls when you need to react to each intermediate screenshot.

3. **Then step B (3D).** That's a new design question (new dependency three.js/React Three Fiber in Rowboat, spheres per level instead of rings, camera and controls). I'll start it with a short design round as before, building on the same data and forces.

content.text:
Fair point: **there is no 3D graph yet.** This screenshot is step A, the 2D version, as planned. 3D was always step B. And step A doesn't convince either:
- **What works:** Company sits in the centre, domains and areas form the core, and colour now follows the domain (purple = product, orange = delivery …).
- **What doesn't work:** The rings are practically invisible, and the large note clusters still drift outward as blobs. The repulsion between 288 nodes beats my ring force. The 2D picture doesn't really show the hierarchy.

So I suggest not polishing 2D any further and going straight to **3D**:

**Proposal for 3D (step B)**
- **Library:** `react-force-graph-3d`, built on three.js and d3-force-3d. It has a built-in hierarchy mode, `dagMode: 'radialout'`. It places nodes along their `parent` edges in **spherical shells per level** around the company, with physics, drag, orbit and zoom. Exactly the "3D hierarchy" without writing our own engine.
- **Data:** We reuse what step A already produces (`level`, `parentId`, `domain`, typed edges). Parent edges define the shells; relations are coloured lines, body links faint.
- **UI:** a **2D | 3D toggle** in the Brain graph. 3D is the default as soon as the vault has hierarchy data. Click a node → opens the note as before. Hover → name and type.
- **Cost:** new dependencies in the Rowboat renderer (`three`, `react-force-graph-3d`, ~1 MB). That makes the patch a bit bigger.
- **Alternative:** our own React Three Fiber scene with the step A forces in 3D. More control, but considerably more code. I'd only take it if the library falls short.

**Shall I build 3D this way?** I'd do it on the same branch `ehl-schema-graph`, with tests for the data mapping and a check by screenshot, and open the PR only after that.

content.text:
I've built and committed the 3D view (commit `2453c4d` on `ehl-schema-graph`, not pushed yet).

**What it does:**
- **3D, rotatable:** drag with the mouse to rotate, scroll to zoom, right-drag to pan.
- **Hierarchy as spheres:** Company sits in the centre. Each level is its own **sphere shell** around it:
  - domains on the 1st shell,
  - areas on the 2nd,
  - notes on the 3rd/4th.

  Parent lines hold subtrees together.
- **Lines and labels:** relations show as **orange** lines (name on hover), body links stay faint. Hovering over a node shows its name; clicking opens the note.
- **2D/3D toggle** in the top right. 3D is the default as soon as the vault has hierarchy data, and the old 2D graph is still there.
- three.js only loads when the 3D view is opened, so the rest of Rowboat doesn't get slower.

**Tested:**
- 22 tests for the graph logic, including 3 new ones for the 3D data.
- Typecheck clean.
- The renderer suite failed 3 hook tests (`use-space-boards`) in the full run under load. Run on their own, all 3 pass. They have nothing to do with the graph.
- What I couldn't test myself: what it actually looks like.

**Please:**
1. Press **Ctrl+R** in the Rowboat window. Vite has to pick up the new 3D library; the first load can take a few seconds.
2. Open **Brain → Graph** and send me a screenshot.

If an error shows up instead of the graph, I'll restart Rowboat.

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

   **Original goal (10 Oct)**
   - Turn Rowboat into a project-management tool for EHL Munich 2026, a hackathon with a 6-min pitch on 11 Oct.
   - The pieces:
     - Marketing (vibemind-os/spaces/marketing) produces data and branding.
     - Sales (sales-claw) enters contacts.
     - Rowboat gives the overview and manages things (e.g. when what is sent).
   - Constraints:
     - Rowboat should run on the members' PCs.
     - Data from the other deployments flows in.
     - Only the user's own claw is synced.

   **Submission work (11 Oct)**
   - Dependencies/install script, README, a "why Rowboat as open source" explanation, docs for the 3D car engine, a step-by-step walkthrough.
   - English language; Apache license like Rowboat.
   - Download the 3D cars; include them in the repo.
   - Push the demo video.
   - Laura MCP integrated into Rowboat (`~/.rowboat-ehl/config/mcp.json`).
   - Push to main via PR (admin merge approved by the user, "mach für mich von mir freigebene felix", then option 2 = permission rule).

   **Sub-project 1 – vault schema**
   - One uniform, extensible, maintainable hierarchy for ALL business data of an AI company, usable by graph, AI and humans.
   - The user rejected inference-only hierarchy ("für ein Projekt managment tool müsste es doch eine Einheitliche Hiearchie geben...") and wanted finance and other company areas.
   - "erst filesystem genau planen", "/iter 3 mal" over which areas an AI company needs.

   **Sub-project 2 – brain graph**
   - Rowboat's brain graph should show the hierarchy. The user chose option B: modify Rowboat's own `graph-view.tsx` in the fork.
   - Layout "C a" = force + radial rings.
   - Then the user explicitly wanted **3D** ("ok and then 3d", "wo ist da den bitte ein 3 D graph?", "das ist doch flat").
   - Feedback on 3D: "der wackelt wenn ich den orbit bewege. und der abstand zwischen den nodes könnte mehr sein."
   - Most recent request: **"restart rowboat"**.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Rowboat Desktop** (rowboatlabs/rowboat, Apache-2.0).
     - Team fork Flissel/rowboat, branch `ehl` pinned to upstream `72e9d8c`.
     - Local clone at `C:\Users\User\Desktop\rowboat`, origin = Flissel/rowboat.
     - Electron app in `apps/x`, renderer = React + Vite + vitest (jsdom) + pnpm.
     - Dev run: `npm run dev` with `ROWBOAT_WORKDIR=~/.rowboat-ehl`.
   - **Rowboat extension points:**
     - `<workdir>/apps/torque` (the Torque app)
     - `knowledge/` vault (Markdown, `[[Folder/Name]]` links, exact-path resolution)
     - `config/notes.json` note types
     - `config/mcp.json`
     - app host API `/_rowboat/llm/generate`, `/_rowboat/data/*`
   - **Rowboat internals learned:**
     - Built-in folders People/Organizations/Projects/Topics/Meetings/Agent Notes/Voice Memos are hard-coded in prompts.
     - The type `folder` in notes.json is effectively ignored.
     - The properties editor drops nested YAML.
     - `Agent Notes/inbox.md`, `user.md`, `preferences.md` are Rowboat memory files: the inbox is consumed line by line; user/preferences are injected raw into the chat prompt.
     - The graph groups by first path segment.
   - **Vault schema design:**
     - 15 L1 domains (12 business + 3 cross-cutting): strategy, legal, finance, team, sales, success, partners, marketing, product, ai, delivery, operations, register, sources, knowledge.
     - 56 L2 areas.
     - Levels L0 Company, L1 Domains, L2 Areas, L3 entity, L4 detail.
     - Flat type folders (F1).
     - Flat front matter: `id`, `type`, `domain`, `level`, `parent` (one quoted link) plus 12 relations: works_at, contact_at, investor_in, candidate_for, customer, project, product, owner, about, evidence, executed_by, when.
     - One vault per tenant; private data in a separate vault.
     - Parent rule `parent level ≤ note level`.
     - Hub rule for same-type parents.
   - **3D graph:**
     - react-force-graph-3d 1.29.0 + three 0.180.0 + d3-force-3d 3.0.6 (+ @types/three 0.180.0 dev).
     - `forceRadial` per level gives sphere shells.

83	      force.y += Math.cos(own) * push
84	    }
85	    forces.set(node.id, force)
86	  }

90	/** Start positions: every node with a level on its ring, each subtree inside its parent's angular sector
91	 * (sector size ∝ subtree size). Roots share the full circle. Cycles are cut. */
92	export function initialHierarchyPositions(
93	  nodes: LevelNode[],
94	  ringSpacing: number = DEFAULT_FORCES.ringSpacing,
95	): Map<string, Point> {
96	  const leveled = nodes.filter((n) => n.level !== undefined).sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id))
97	  const byId = new Map(leveled.map((n) => [n.id, n]))
98	  const children = new Map<string, string[]>()
99	  const roots: string[] = []
100	  for (const node of leveled) {
101	    if (node.parentId && byId.has(node.parentId)) {
102	      const list = children.get(node.parentId) ?? []
103	      list.push(node.id)
104	      children.set(node.parentId, list)
105	    } else {
106	      roots.push(node.id)
107	    }
108	  }
109	  const sizes = new Map<string, number>()
110	  const sizeOf = (id: string, seen: Set<string>): number => {
111	    const known = sizes.get(id)
112	    if (known !== undefined) return known
113	    if (seen.has(id)) return 1
114	    seen.add(id)
115	    const size = 1 + (children.get(id) ?? []).reduce((sum, child) => sum + sizeOf(child, seen), 0)
116	    sizes.set(id, size)
117	    return size
118	  }
119	  const out = new Map<string, Point>()
120	  const place = (ids: string[], start: number, span: number) => {
121	    const fresh = ids.filter((id) => !out.has(id))
122	    const total = fresh.reduce((sum, id) => sum + sizeOf(id, new Set()), 0)
123	    let angle = start
124	    for (const id of fresh) {
125	      const share = (span * sizeOf(id, new Set())) / total
126	      const mid = angle + share / 2
127	      const radius = (byId.get(id)?.level ?? 0) * ringSpacing
128	      out.set(id, { x: radius * Math.cos(mid), y: radius * Math.sin(mid) })
129	      place(children.get(id) ?? [], angle, share)
130	      angle += share
131	    }
132	  }
133	  place(roots, 0, Math.PI * 2)
134	  for (const node of leveled) {
135	    if (!out.has(node.id)) place([node.id], 0, Math.PI * 2)
136	  }
137	  return out
138	}

140	export type EdgeKind = 'parent' | 'relation' | 'link'
141	export type HierarchyEdge = { source: string; target: string; kind: EdgeKind; relation?: string }
142	export type NodeInfo = { level?: number; parentId?: string; domain?: string }
143	
144	const RANK: Record<EdgeKind, number> = { link: 0, relation: 1, parent: 2 }
145	
146	/** Typed edges (one per unordered pair, strongest kind wins) and hierarchy info per node. */
147	export function buildHierarchyGraph(
148	  contents: { path: string; data: string }[],
149	  nodeSet: Set<string>,
150	  toNodeId: (wikiTarget: string) => string | null,
151	): { edges: HierarchyEdge[]; info: Map<string, NodeInfo> } {
152	  const edges = new Map<string, HierarchyEdge>()
153	  const info = new Map<string, NodeInfo>()
154	  const add = (source: string, rawTarget: string, kind: EdgeKind, relation?: string) => {
155	    const target = toNodeId(rawTarget)
156	    if (!target || target === source || !nodeSet.has(target)) return
157	    const key = source < target ? `${source}|${target}` : `${target}|${source}`
158	    const existing = edges.get(key)
159	    if (existing && RANK[existing.kind] >= RANK[kind]) return
160	    edges.set(key, relation ? { source, target, kind, relation } : { source, target, kind })
161	  }
162	  for (const { path, data } of contents) {
163	    const hierarchy = parseHierarchy(data)
164	    const parentId = hierarchy.parent ? toNodeId(hierarchy.parent) : null
165	    info.set(path, {
166	      level: hierarchy.level,
167	      parentId: parentId && nodeSet.has(parentId) ? parentId : undefined,
168	      domain: hierarchy.domain,
169	    })
170	    if (hierarchy.parent) add(path, hierarchy.parent, 'parent')
171	    for (const relation of hierarchy.relations) add(path, relation.target, 'relation', relation.name)
172	    for (const match of data.matchAll(LINK)) add(path, match[1], 'link')
173	  }
174	  return { edges: Array.from(edges.values()), info }
175	}

177	// ---- 3D view (react-force-graph-3d): nodes on one sphere shell per level ----
178	
179	export type Graph3dNode = { id: string; name: string; color: string; level: number; val: number }
180	export type Graph3dLink = {
181	  source: string
182	  target: string
183	  kind: EdgeKind
184	  relation?: string
185	  width: number
186	  opacity: number
187	}
188	type InNode = { id: string; label: string; color: string; degree: number; level?: number }
189	type InEdge = { source: string; target: string; kind?: EdgeKind; relation?: string }
190	
191	const LINK_STYLE: Record<EdgeKind, { width: number; opacity: number }> = {
192	  parent: { width: 1.2, opacity: 0.6 },
193	  relation: { width: 0.6, opacity: 0.5 },
194	  link: { width: 0, opacity: 0.12 },
195	}
196	
197	/** Distance between two sphere shells in the 3D view (wider than the 2D rings: shells hold more nodes). */
198	export const SHELL_SPACING_3D = 300
199	
200	/** Radius of the sphere shell for a level; level 0 is the centre. */
201	export function shellRadius(level: number, spacing: number = SHELL_SPACING_3D): number {
202	  return level * spacing
203	}
204	
205	/** Graph data for the 3D view. Nodes without a level go one shell beyond the deepest level. */
206	export function toGraph3d(nodes: InNode[], edges: InEdge[]): { nodes: Graph3dNode[]; links: Graph3dLink[] } {
207	  const deepest = nodes.reduce((max, n) => (n.level !== undefined && n.level > max ? n.level : max), 0)
208	  return {
209	    nodes: nodes.map((n) => ({
210	      id: n.id,
211	      name: n.label,
212	      color: n.color,
213	      level: n.level ?? deepest + 1,
214	      val: 1 + Math.min(12, n.degree),
215	    })),
216	    links: edges.map((e) => {
217	      const kind = e.kind ?? 'link'
218	      return { source: e.source, target: e.target, kind, relation: e.relation, ...LINK_STYLE[kind] }
219	    }),
220	  }
221	}
