"""Generate what the schema implies: Company/Domains/Areas notes, the rules note and Rowboat's notes.json."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from pathlib import Path

from .model import STRUCTURE_TYPES, Schema, TypeDef
from .notes import note_text, slug, split

log = logging.getLogger("ehl_schema.build")

MANAGED = "schema"
RULES_NOTE = "Agent Notes/Vault Schema"
RULES_MARK = "\n\nSchema rules ("
GENERIC_BODY = ("# {Title}\n\n## Summary\n{2-3 sentences.}\n\n## Key facts\n{Substantive facts only. Leave empty if "
                "none.}\n\n## Open items\n{Next steps only. Leave empty if none.}\n")


def _front(schema: Schema, **fields) -> dict:
    # the same keys migrate adds to every note, so build and migrate agree and re-runs settle
    return {**fields, "visibility": "team", "env": "prod", "managed_by": MANAGED, "schema_version": schema.version}


def structure_notes(schema: Schema, company: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    notes: dict[str, str] = {}
    domain_links = "\n".join(f"- [[{schema.domain_note(k)}]]" for k in schema.domains)
    notes["Company"] = note_text(
        _front(schema, id="company", type="Company", domain="company", level=0),
        f"# {company}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Company (L0)\n\n## Domains\n{domain_links}\n")
    for key, title in schema.domains.items():
        areas = "\n".join(f"- [[{schema.area_note(a)}]]" for a, d in schema.areas.items() if d == key)
        notes[schema.domain_note(key)] = note_text(
            _front(schema, id=f"domain-{key}", type="Domains", domain=key, level=1, parent="[[Company]]"),
            f"# {title}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Domain (L1)\n**Key:** {key}\n\n## Areas\n{areas}\n")
    for area, key in schema.areas.items():
        types = ", ".join(n for n, td in schema.types.items() if td.default_parent == area) or "none"
        notes[schema.area_note(area)] = note_text(
            _front(schema, id=f"area-{slug(area)}", type="Areas", domain=key, level=2,
                   parent=f"[[{schema.domain_note(key)}]]"),
            f"# {area}\n\n## Info\n**Type:** Area (L2)\n**Domain:** [[{schema.domain_note(key)}]]\n"
            f"**Note types placed here by default:** {types}\n")
    td = schema.types["Agent Notes"]
    notes[RULES_NOTE] = note_text(
        _front(schema, id="agent-notes-vault-schema", type="Agent Notes", domain=td.domain, level=td.level,
               parent=f"[[{schema.area_note(td.default_parent)}]]"),
        rules_body(schema))
    return notes


def rules_body(schema: Schema) -> str:
    lines = [f"# Vault schema (v{schema.version})", "",
             "Generated from schema/vault-schema.yaml by `ehl-schema build`. Do not edit; change the schema file.", "",
             "## Front matter", "",
             "Every note starts with flat YAML front matter. Required keys: id, type, domain, level, parent.",
             "- `id`: a stable slug; never change it. `type`: the folder name. `level`: from the table below.",
             '- `parent`: exactly one quoted link, for example `parent: "[[Areas/Pipeline]]"`.',
             '- Relations are lists of quoted links with the full path, for example `about: ["[[Areas/Pipeline]]"]`.',
             "- Never nest keys. Optional: status, visibility (team | restricted), env (prod | test), when (YYYY-MM-DD).",
             "", "## Domains and areas", "", "| Domain | Key | Areas |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for key, title in schema.domains.items():
        areas = ", ".join(a for a, d in schema.areas.items() if d == key)
        lines.append(f"| {title} | {key} | {areas} |")
    lines += ["", "## Note types", "",
              "| Type (folder) | Domain | Level | Parent (in order) | Default area | Required | Optional |",
              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for name, td in schema.types.items():
        if name in STRUCTURE_TYPES:
            continue
        domain = "from its parent area" if td.domain == "*" else td.domain
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {domain} | {td.level} | {', '.join(td.parent)} | {td.default_parent or ''} | "
                     f"{', '.join(td.required) or '–'} | {', '.join(td.optional) or '–'} |")
    lines += ["", "## Relations", "", "| Key | Points to |", "|---|---|"]
    for name, rel in schema.relations.items():
        target = "a date" if rel.kind == "date" else ("any note" if rel.targets is None else ", ".join(rel.targets))
        lines.append(f"| {name} | {target} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def write_structure(schema: Schema, vault: Path, company: str) -> int:
    written = 0
    for path, text in structure_notes(schema, company).items():
        file = vault / f"{path}.md"
        if file.exists():
            old = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            if old == text:
                continue
            front, _, _ = split(old)
            if (front or {}).get("managed_by") != MANAGED:
                log.warning("%s exists and is not managed by the schema; left as it is", file)
                continue
        file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        file.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
        written += 1
    return written


def _parent_hint(td: TypeDef) -> str:
    if td.parent == ("Areas",):
        return f"Areas/{td.default_parent}"
    options = ", ".join(f"{p}/…" for p in td.parent if p != "Areas")
    return f"one of: {options}" + (f" (else Areas/{td.default_parent})" if td.default_parent else "")


def _skeleton(schema: Schema, td: TypeDef) -> str:
    lines = ["---", "id: {slug of the title}", f"type: {td.name}", f"domain: {td.domain}", f"level: {td.level}",
             f'parent: "[[{{{_parent_hint(td)}}}]]"']
    for name in td.required:
        rel = schema.relations[name]
        if rel.kind == "date":
            lines.append(f"{name}: {{YYYY-MM-DD}}")
        else:
            target = rel.targets[0] if rel.targets else "Folder"
            lines.append(f'{name}: ["[[{{{target}/…}}]]"]')
    lines += [f"schema_version: {schema.version}", "---", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _guide(schema: Schema, td: TypeDef) -> str:
    default = f" (else [[Areas/{td.default_parent}]])" if td.default_parent else ""
    return (f"v{schema.version}): flat YAML front matter. type: {td.name}; domain: {td.domain}; level: {td.level}; "
            f"id: a stable slug, never change it. parent: exactly one quoted link to a note of type "
            f"{', '.join(td.parent)}{default}. Required relations: {', '.join(td.required) or 'none'}. "
            f"Optional relations: {', '.join(td.optional) or 'none'}. Relation values are lists of quoted "
            f'full-path links like ["[[Organizations/Acme]]"]. Status: {", ".join(td.statuses) or "free text"}.')


def _strip_front(template: str) -> str:
    """The template body without a leading --- block. Text-based: template placeholders are not always YAML."""
    t = template.replace("\r\n", "\n")
    if t.startswith("---\n"):
        end = t.find("\n---\n", 3)
        if end != -1:
            return t[end + 5:]
    return t


def notes_json(schema: Schema, existing: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    by_type = {e["type"]: dict(e) for e in existing if isinstance(e, dict) and "type" in e}
    order = [e["type"] for e in existing if isinstance(e, dict) and "type" in e]
    for name, td in schema.types.items():
        if name in STRUCTURE_TYPES or td.domain == "*" or (td.builtin and name not in by_type):
            continue
        entry = by_type.get(name, {"type": name, "folder": name, "template": "", "extractionGuide": ""})
        if name not in by_type:
            order.append(name)
        template = entry.get("template") or ""
        if not (td.builtin and not template.strip()):
            body = _strip_front(template)
            body = body if body.strip() else (td.template or GENERIC_BODY)
            entry["template"] = _skeleton(schema, td) + body
        guide = (entry.get("extractionGuide") or "").split(RULES_MARK)[0]
        entry["extractionGuide"] = guide + RULES_MARK + _guide(schema, td)
        by_type[name] = entry
    return [by_type[name] for name in order]


def build(schema: Schema, workdir: Path, company: str) -> dict:
    written = write_structure(schema, workdir / "knowledge", company)
    config = workdir / "config" / "notes.json"
    if not config.exists():
        log.warning("%s does not exist yet: start Rowboat once, then run build again", config)
        return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "missing"}
    old = config.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    new = json.dumps(notes_json(schema, json.loads(old)), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
    if new == old:
        return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "unchanged"}
    config.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return {"notes": written, "notes_json": "updated"}

import json
import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from .build import write_structure
from .issues import Issue
from .model import Schema

from .profile import Profile

log = logging.getLogger("ehl_schema.vaultmap")

MAP_FILE = Path("config") / "vault-map.json"
MAP_VERSION = 1


@dataclass
class MapResult:
    structure: int
    notes: int
    excluded: int
    issues: list[Issue]
    written: bool


def map_document(company: str, res: Resolution) -> dict:
    notes = {path: {"type": p.type, "level": p.level, "domain": p.domain, "parent": p.parent}
             for path, p in sorted(res.placements.items())}
    return {"version": MAP_VERSION, "company": company,
            "generated_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), "notes": notes}


def _same(old_text: str, doc: dict) -> bool:
    try:
        old = json.loads(old_text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return False
    if not isinstance(old, dict):
        return False

def write_map(workdir: Path, doc: dict) -> bool:
    file = workdir / MAP_FILE
    if file.exists() and _same(file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), doc):
        return False

Use `--skip-rag` to run without Docker and OpenAI. Nordi then answers from Torque's data only.

The three 3D cars ship with the repo (`demo/torque/dist/visu/models/`), so nothing has to be downloaded.
**One manual step:** start the demo, then add your own model API key in Rowboat → Settings.

```bash
python scripts/install.py --start
```

`--start` launches Rowboat (dev mode), the RAG backend and both syncs. The first build takes a few minutes.
Then open **Apps → Torque**. If you already use Rowboat, the demo keeps its data in `~/.rowboat-ehl`, so
your own `~/.rowboat` stays untouched.

Team members setting up a development PC (forks, work-package branches) use [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) and
`scripts/setup_pc.py` instead.

first; it backs the vault up to `~/.rowboat/knowledge.bak-<time>`.

# Torque in Rowboat: an AI product requirements cockpit EHL Munich 2026 Grand Finale (10–11 Oct 2026, Garching). Product managers choose what the successor of a car should have. Their inputs are thousands of customer comments, survey studies, option price lists, sales figures and market research. **Torque** turns these inputs into a ranked list of purchase drivers and requirements. Every requirement carries its evidence, an explicit human decision and an append-only audit trail. On a 3D model of the car you can see which parts customers criticise. Torque runs as an app inside **[Rowboat](https://github.com/rowboatlabs/rowboat)**, the open-source AI coworker. Rowboat's knowledge graph and agent work on the same data as the cockpit. **Demo video (83 s):** [docs/media/demo.mp4](docs/media/demo.mp4). It shows Torque in Rowboat, the Concept 3D heat map, the market MCP in Rowboat's chat, the market map and the Nordi copilot. The voice-over is AI-generated. ## What the challenge asks for, and where to see it | Deliverable | In the prototype | | --- | --- | | 1. Prototype that processes heterogeneous inputs, derives and prioritises requirements, with human review | **Torque**: *Overview*, *Purchase drivers*, *Simulator*. Inputs: feedback workbooks, customer studies, option lists and sales volumes in `Dataset/`, plus outside market data via the `ehl-market` MCP server | | 2. Structured list of requirements: ID, description, findings and sources, priority or score, rationale, evidence level, assumptions, decision status | **Rowboat vault** `Requirements/` (one note per requirement, e.g. `R-01 Fast charging`: target, acceptance criterion, assumptions) and **Torque** *Purchase drivers* (score, evidence, quotes with comment IDs). The *Brief* export compiles all of it | | 3. End-to-end workflow: what the AI does autonomously, where a human must decide | **Torque** *Data and workflow*: every step from ingest to decision, marked "autonomous, logged" or "human". Spec: [docs/deliverables.md](docs/deliverables.md) | | 4. Audit trail from findings through scoring to the human decision | **Torque** *Audit trail* (append-only: content, score, priority, evidence and status changes with actor, time and reason) and *Review log*. Decisions are written back to Rowboat notes (`Purchase Drivers/`) | ## How it fits together ```mermaid flowchart LR D[Dataset/
feedback, studies,
option lists, sales] --> P[research pipeline
clean, mask PII, merge] D --> V[demo/visu
heat map scores] P --> M[ehl-market

[Why Rowboat](docs/why-rowboat.md) - **Torque** (`demo/torque/`) is the decision cockpit. It is a single-file web app; its source is `demo/torque/dist/index.html`. Two syncs keep it and the vault in step: decisions go to notes, and notes go to the cockpit. - **Concept 3D** (`demo/visu/`, React Three Fiber + three.js) colours the parts of the successor car by customer sentiment and takes design prompts. [The 3D engine](docs/3d-engine.md) - **Nordi**, Torque's copilot, answers from the data on screen and, with the RAG backend, from the indexed source documents (`app.py`, `src/rag_backend/`, Qdrant). - **ehl-market** (`market/`) is an MCP server for Rowboat's agent: sources, live World Bank, Eurostat and NHTSA data, correlation tools. ## Run it You need Git, Python 3.12, Node.js 22 (or 24.15+), pnpm 10 and, for the RAG, Docker Desktop. The installer checks these and tells you how to install what is missing (winget on Windows, Homebrew on macOS). ```bash python scripts/install.py --check ``` ```bash python scripts/install.py ``` The installer does all of this and is safe to re-run: - clones Rowboat (`Flissel/rowboat`, branch `ehl`) next to this repo and installs its packages; - sets up the market MCP server and the research pipeline; - writes Torque's customer quotes from `Dataset/`; - fills Rowboat's knowledge vault and registers Torque as a Rowboat app; - adds `ehl-market` to Rowboat's `mcp.json`; - starts Qdrant, asks for `OPENAI_API_KEY` (written to `search/.env`, gitignored) and builds the search index. Use `--skip-rag` to run without Docker and OpenAI. Nordi then answers from Torque's data only. The three 3D cars ship with the repo (`demo/torque/dist/visu/models/`), so nothing has to be downloaded. **One manual step:** start the demo, then add your own model API key in Rowboat → Settings. ```bash python scripts/install.py --start ``` `--start` launches Rowboat (dev mode), the RAG backend and both syncs. The first build takes a few minutes. Then open **Apps → Torque**. If you already use Rowboat, the demo keeps its data in `~/.rowboat-ehl`, so your own `~/.rowboat` stays untouched. Team members setting up a development PC (forks, work-package branches) use [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) and `scripts/setup_pc.py` instead. ## Repository | Path | What | | --- | --- | | `demo/torque/` | Torque app: `dist/index.html` (the cockpit), `rowboat-app.json` (app manifest), `sync.py` (cockpit ↔ vault), `make_quotes.py` | | `demo/visu/` | Concept 3D engine (React Three Fiber, built into `demo/torque/dist/visu/`), heat map scoring (`feedback.py`), vault notes and sync (`vault.py`, `brand.py`, `assumptions.py`, `generate_texts.py`) | | `research/` | Data pipeline: cleaning, PII masking, clustering, findings | | `market/` | `ehl-market` MCP server for Rowboat's agent | | `schema/` | Vault schema: one hierarchy for all business data (`vault-schema.yaml`), and `ehl-schema build \| lint \| migrate` ([spec](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-vault-schema-design.md)) | | `app.py`, `src/rag_backend/`, `scripts/` | RAG backend (FastAPI, Qdrant, OpenAI embeddings) and its ingest scripts; `scripts/install.py` | | `Dataset/` | Challenge data (F70, G60, G68, G70), test data | | `outputs/` | Preprocessed Markdown, chunks and embeddings for the RAG | | `docs/` | Deliverables, data pipeline, RAG backend, design specs, and the pages below | ### Nordi voice (mic and read aloud) In Torque's chat, the **mic** button records a question. Click it again to stop; the question is transcribed and sent to Nordi. The **speaker** button reads answers aloud and stays on until you turn it off. Speech uses Rowboat's voice API if it is configured. Otherwise it uses the RAG backend (`/voice/transcribe`, `/voice/tts`, OpenAI key from `search/.env`), so keep the backend running on :8100. Allow microphone access when asked. Nordi answers from Torque's dataset numbers plus RAG passages. When the two disagree, the dataset numbers win. Markets where a model is not sold show N/A, and Nordi says when the answer is not in the data. ## Docs - [Why Rowboat, and how we integrated it](docs/why-rowboat.md) - [The 3D engine](docs/3d-engine.md) - [Walkthrough: the app step by step](docs/walkthrough.md) - [Deliverables](docs/deliverables.md): the challenge brief, requirement and audit-log schemas, and the split between AI and human work - [Data pipeline plan](docs/data-pipeline-plan.md) · [RAG backend](docs/rag-backend.md) · [Market MCP](market/README.md) ## Team GitHub: [Flissel](https://github.com/Flissel) (orchestrator) · [PedroLemonade](https://github.com/PedroLemonade) · [yunes-mahan](https://github.com/yunes-mahan) · [syed-rayyanadil](https://github.com/syed-rayyanadil) · [Paolabeiia](https://github.com/Paolabeiia).
